source.title: Towards Interpretable Hallucination Analysis and Mitigation in LVLMs via Contrastive Neuron Steering
source.authors: Guangtao Lyu; Xinyi Cheng; Qi Liu; Chenghao Xu; Jiexi Yan; Muli Yang; Fen Fang; Cheng Deng

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present. Some figures and tables are flattened in the web extraction, but the relevant text descriptions and Table 1 values are readable.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether sparse, interpretable features can be recovered and used in real multimodal models, applying SAEs to LVLM visual encoders rather than reproducing the original toy-network method.
record.gate_note: The paper analyzes SAE visual features and their representation of concepts, so those results bear on V4 and V5. The hallucination benchmark results for CNS are not rows: they measure the performance of an intervention, not whether the claimed representation units exist. The paper's concept-steering examples are included only where they report how many SAE neurons were needed to control a concept.
record.test_reason: The paper uses a Matryoshka BatchTopK SAE on the LLaVA-1.5 visual encoder as a tool for analysing and mitigating hallucinations. Its quantitative results are hallucination and general benchmark scores for its own CNS method. Its claims about SAE features are asserted from top-16 image visualizations, plus a count of always-on neurons. It gives no recovery, interpretability or monosemanticity score, no comparison against neurons or random dictionaries, and no test of completeness or stability. The subject is a vision encoder, not an LLM. The steering examples are single anecdotes that report steering magnitudes, not a measure of whether features are the model's units.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors' central conclusions are that hallucinations arise mainly from disrupted or spurious activations of image-specific SAE neurons, with always-on neurons stable and of little influence. They also conclude that their CNS method (contrastive clean-vs-noisy neuron steering at prefill) reduces hallucinations across five LVLMs while preserving general benchmark performance.
record.recipe_differences: The original source studies superposition in toy networks. This paper trains Matryoshka BatchTopK SAEs on LVLM visual-encoder features, then analyzes and steers those features; it does not test toy-model superposition geometry or sparsity transitions.
record.method_sensitivity: Concept steering varies with scene complexity and the number of neurons edited; the paper reports that multi-neuron steering can be more effective in complex scenes.

fits_no_version.finding: In one LLaVA-1.5 example, the 'dog' concept is spread over several SAE latents (breeds, poses, context). Removing it needs α=−100 on one latent versus α=−10 each on three; inserting it in a complex scene needs α=500 on one latent versus α=20 each on three.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Single SAE latents in vision encoders may not each capture a whole concept; concepts can split hierarchically across latents, affecting steering.

fits_no_version.finding: About 10 of 65k SAE latents are in the Top-20 for every COCO image. They encode textures or colour regions, and zeroing them barely changes POPE accuracy (84.68 vs 84.63 baseline), while zeroing image-specific latents drops it to 63.08.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAEs on vision encoders contain a small set of dense, input-invariant latents, possibly related to register or massive activations.

record.problems: The feature characterization is primarily qualitative, with no reported numerical score for recovery completeness, feature stability, or semantic purity. The steering examples demonstrate controllability under intervention rather than the prevalence of those representations in unmanipulated outputs.
record.rows_left_out: Hallucination and general-benchmark metrics (Tables 2–8) were left out because they evaluate CNS or model task performance rather than feature recovery or whether SAE features are complete canonical units. Noise-related performance and neuron-change results (Figure 3) were also left out because they do not measure the versions' named feature geometry or unit completeness.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, geometry or sparsity transition.
All: no capacity or importance analysis.
No LLM layers. Feature recoverability in the vision encoder is asserted from visualizations, not measured, and there is no neuron-level polysemanticity comparison.
Completeness, stability across seeds or sizes, and canonicality are not evaluated. Only anecdotal observations show one concept (dog) spread over several SAE latents.

missing.what: Table 1 zeroing results. POPE accuracy/F1: baseline 84.63/84.99, always-on zeroed 84.68/85.08, image-specific zeroed 63.08/57.36, random 84.31/84.65. This is a functional test of SAE latent types, if rows are later linked.

record.verdict_notes: Reclassified from tests/T3 to uses_without_test/T4. The SAE is the analysis tool, and its interpretability is assumed and illustrated, not tested. The setting is a vision encoder, not an LLM, so V4 as worded does not apply. There are no verdict labels. The steering anecdotes are recorded under fits_no_version.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, overcomplete sparse feature storage, near-orthogonal geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometric structure.
Whether limited capacity causes polysemanticity, or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions while others share.
Whether polysemanticity arises for reasons other than capacity pressure, and whether it is evidence of superposition.
The study examines SAE features in LVLM visual encoders, not feature distribution across neurons in LLM language-model layers generally.
The study does not directly evaluate completeness, stability across training or model changes, or whether SAE features are a canonical basis.
It does not compare one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional feature representations.

rows.subject: LLaVA-1.5
rows.operation_detail: Counted neurons that appeared in the Top-20 across images at image level.
rows.measure: Number of always-on neurons among 65k SAE neurons
rows.value: 10 out of 65k consistently appear in the Top-20 across all images
rows.note: The authors describe the remaining image-specific neurons as selective and semantically meaningful; this row records the separately reported always-on count.
rows.check: The always-on count (10 of 65k in the Top-20 for all images) is a descriptive statistic of SAE activations. It is not evidence that the model's features are sparse or distributed across neurons, and no baseline exists.

rows.subject: LLaVA-1.5
rows.operation_detail: Analyzed top-activated SAE neurons and their visualizations at image and patch levels.
rows.value: Image-specific neurons activate strongly for visually similar images and capture semantically meaningful, localized concepts at patch level; visualizations show neurons associated with concrete objects and patterns.
rows.note: Qualitative characterization; the paper does not report a numerical feature-recovery or semantic-purity score.
rows.check: The evidence is qualitative top-activating image visualizations in a CLIP-style vision encoder, not an LLM. The authors treat interpretability as confirmed rather than measuring it, with no score and no comparison to raw neurons.

rows.subject: LLaVA-1.5
rows.operation_detail: Amplified a single dog-related neuron to insert the dog concept into a caption.
rows.measure: Whether the dog concept appeared in the output
rows.note: A single neuron could control a concept in this simple scene; the paper states that steering difficulty depends on scene complexity and concept distribution.
rows.check: This is a single anecdotal steering example. The α needed to insert a concept measures steering ease, not whether SAE features are complete, stable or canonical units. The text describes α=50 as modest and the concept as appearing, so state 'partial' is unsupported.

rows.subject: LLaVA-1.5
rows.operation_detail: Amplified a single dog-related neuron to insert the concept.
rows.measure: Whether the dog concept appeared in the output
rows.value: A very large weight, α = 500, was needed for a visible effect.
rows.note: The authors contrast this with coordinated adjustment of several dog-related neurons in the same complex-scene analysis.
rows.check: An anecdotal steering magnitude (α=500 in a complex scene). It does not measure the V5 properties.

rows.subject: LLaVA-1.5
rows.operation_detail: Coordinated amplification of three dog-related neurons to insert the concept.
rows.measure: Whether the dog concept appeared in the output
rows.value: Natural insertions were obtained with α = 20 for each neuron.
rows.note: The authors report that coordinated steering of multiple concept-related neurons was more stable and natural than steering a single neuron in this complex scene.
rows.check: Anecdotal multi-neuron steering (α=20 each). It is a comparison of steering strategies, not a measure of unit completeness.

rows.subject: LLaVA-1.5
rows.operation_detail: Suppressed a single dog-related neuron to remove the concept from a caption.

conditions.value: Complex scene containing a dog and chair

rows.measure: Whether the dog concept was removed from the output
rows.value: A very large negative weight, α = −100, was needed before the concept disappeared.
rows.note: The paper describes dog-related concepts as distributed across neurons for different breeds, poses, and contextual cues.
rows.check: Anecdotal suppression magnitude (α=−100). It bears at most indirectly on concept splitting across SAE features.

rows.subject: LLaVA-1.5
rows.operation_detail: Jointly suppressed three dog-related neurons to remove the concept.

conditions.value: Complex scene containing a dog and chair

rows.measure: Whether the dog concept was removed from the output
rows.value: The concept was removed more naturally and reliably with α = −10 for each neuron.
rows.note: Supports the paper's account that complex concepts may be distributed over several SAE neurons; it does not establish that the SAE basis is complete or canonical.
rows.check: Anecdotal joint suppression (α=−10 each). It does not measure V5's named properties.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: LLaVA-1.5 visual encoder representations analyzed on COCO
reader_labels.reason: The authors identify sparse SAE neurons with image-level and localized semantic content, including a reported set of 10 always-on neurons among 65k; see r1–r2.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Concept steering in simple versus complex visual scenes
reader_labels.reason: A single neuron can control a concept in a simple scene, but complex scenes can require coordinated edits to multiple neurons, limiting the idea that one SAE feature is a complete, stable unit for a concept; see r3–r7.
